parts.title: New Understanding of Giraffes in the Wild
parts.article:
(A) Even as the tallest animals on Earth, giraffes can be easy to overlook. Despite being a favorite in zoos, until recently almost nobody studied giraffes in the wild. ‘When I first became interested in giraffes in 2008 and started looking through the scientific literature, I was really surprised to see how little had been done,’ said Megan Strauss, an animal researcher at the University of Minnesota, USA. All that is changing fast, as a growing number of researchers seek to understand the biology and complex behavior of this graceful giant in its native habitat.

(B) Giraffes, found throughout sub-Saharan Africa, are currently classified as a single species with up to nine varieties that differ by features like head shape and whether the fur on their legs is plain or patterned. The giraffe is listed as endangered, but researchers point to evidence that in the past 15 years, the population has fallen some 40 percent.

(C) Recent studies have allowed researchers new insights into giraffes’ social structure. Groups of female giraffes, for example, have been found to form close friendships that can last for years. ‘We’re just at the beginnings of trying to understand this kind of behavior,’ Dr Strauss said. Female giraffes can live 20 years or more, and it makes sense they might rely on each other for clues to the best feeding grounds, help with taking care of their young, or the reduction of stress, by staying in groups.

(D) Mother giraffes have displayed signs of grief after losing their young, known as calves, to lions. Dr Strauss described one case in which a mother spent four days at the place where a lion had eaten her calf, refusing food, and often in the company of two other adult females. Giraffe calves are extremely vulnerable to predators, and though mothers will fight valiantly to keep their young alive — kicking forward and backward — half of all calves are killed in their first year of life.

(E) Male giraffes, known as bulls, generally become more important with age, and older bulls display that dominance physically and behaviorally: as their neck muscles grow, the male’s posture becomes prouder and more vertical. Recent observations show young bulls, when left on their own, mimicking their elders: head held high and neck puffed out. But should a dominant older bull come into view, the younger males instantly try to make themselves look small and innocent.

(F) The younger bulls have reason to fear their elders. Clashes have been witnessed between adults when each bull repeatedly ‘necks’ the other, using his massive neck to slam his head against his rival. One bull somehow survived with a broken neck.

(G) The skin of a giraffe is mostly gray. The coat has dark patches separated by light hair, which serves as camouflage, allowing them to blend in with the light and shade patterns of the acacia trees from which they feed. Grazing giraffes are hard to see even a few meters away.

(H) Research indicates that giraffes also have excellent sight, can see in color and over great distances, which helps them to spot lions and keep track of each other. In addition, a giraffe’s extraordinary mouth has lips and tongue that can together grasp a branch and then pluck away the leaves while avoiding thorns, almost as humans would grab with their hands. Each day, a giraffe consumes about 30 kilograms of leaves, shoots and vines, all digested in its four-chambered stomach.

(I) A giraffe can stand more than six meters tall, with its neck accounting for roughly a third of its height and its legs the same. The giraffe’s long neck is due to the length of the vertebrae, not the number of vertebrae. The growth of the neck largely takes place during early childhood, as giraffe mothers would have a difficult time giving birth to young with longer necks. The giraffe’s head and neck are held up by large muscles attached to the lower spine.

(J) Recent studies show that the greatest challenge to a giraffe’s cardiovascular system is how to both pump blood very high and retrieve it from far below. The outside of a giraffe’s veins are extremely thick, to prevent blood leaking into surrounding tissue. Other adaptations in the cardiovascular system allow the giraffe to bend over for a drink of water, and then raise its head again quickly without fainting.

(K) Researchers were also surprised to find that a giraffe does not have an unusually large heart. It is half a percent of body mass, the same as in a mouse. Moreover, the amount of blood pumped into circulation is modest, proportionally lower than it is in humans. That could help explain why giraffes rarely run for very long: enough oxygen cannot be delivered to their muscles fast enough for them to keep running. Or maybe the giraffes are worried about tripping over their own feet. This is because signals from the nerves travel at about the same speed in giraffes as in rats or other mammals. Given the greater distance they have to travel in the giraffe to reach the brain, it is possible the giraffe faces real challenges in reacting quickly to a rock beneath its hoof or a bite to its ankle.

(L) New understanding of this wonderful animal sheds light on both its physiology and its behavior. Researchers hope to use this knowledge to increase their ability to work with preservation, as its habitat is reduced and the giraffe becomes scarcer.
parts.questions:
Questions 1–7
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1–7 on your answer sheet, write.

Q1 The amount of research on giraffes in their natural environment has increased lately.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q2 Megan Strauss disapproves of keeping giraffes in zoos.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q3 The number of giraffes in Africa has nearly doubled.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q4 Female giraffes tend to live longer than males.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q5 Mother giraffes sometimes use their legs to defend their young.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q6 Younger bulls hold their necks higher in the presence of more powerful males.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q7 Male giraffes have been observed fighting.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN
Questions 8–13
Complete the table below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 8-13 on your answer sheet.
Giraffes: body structure
Physical features Study findings
Skin/coat
  • provides when standing near trees
Eyes
  • allow them to look out for lions
Mouth
  • can be used like to get leaves
Neck
  • about equal in length to the legs
  • length develops in childhood to provide an easier for mothers
Cardiovascular system
  • extra-strong keep blood from spilling into other tissues
  • normal size for such a large animal
Nerves
  • slower reaction time because need to go farther to the brain

reference:
Q1

干扰 你可能看到第1句说“以前几乎没人研究”，但要注意第3句强调了“这一切正在快速改变”（All that is changing fast），一定要往后读完完整语义。

句子 Despite being a favorite in zoos, until recently almost nobody studied giraffes in the wild. ‘When I first became interested in giraffes in 2008 and started looking through the scientific literature, I was really surprised to see how little had been done,’ said Megan Strauss, an animal researcher at the University of Minnesota, USA. All that is changing fast, as a growing number of researchers seek to understand the biology and complex behavior of this graceful giant in its native habitat.

解析 文章明确说到现在越来越多的研究人员正在努力了解野外长颈鹿的行为，这说明野外研究的数量确实增加了。

Q2

解析 原文只提到了Megan对过去很少有人研究野生长颈鹿感到惊讶，根本没提她个人赞不赞成把长颈鹿关在动物园里。

干扰 看到第1句有“zoos”（动物园）这个词，不要自己脑补Megan反对动物园，文章根本没提她的态度，选NOT GIVEN。

句子 Despite being a favorite in zoos, until recently almost nobody studied giraffes in the wild. ‘When I first became interested in giraffes in 2008 and started looking through the scientific literature, I was really surprised to see how little had been done,’ said Megan Strauss, an animal researcher at the University of Minnesota, USA. All that is changing fast, as a growing number of researchers seek to understand the biology and complex behavior of this graceful giant in its native habitat.

Q3

解析 原文清楚地写着过去15年长颈鹿的数量下降了（fallen）约40%，而不是几乎翻倍（doubled）。

干扰 别把“fallen”（下降）看成了增加或者翻倍，数字走向完全相反。

句子 The giraffe is listed as endangered, but researchers point to evidence that in the past 15 years, the population has fallen some 40 percent.

Q4

干扰 你可能看到提到了具体的年龄“20年”，但这不代表有对比，没有提到雄性能活多久就果断选NOT GIVEN。

解析 文章只说雌性长颈鹿能活20年甚至更久，但根本没有把它们的寿命和雄性进行比较。

句子 Female giraffes can live 20 years or more, and it makes sense they might rely on each other for clues to the best feeding grounds, help with taking care of their young, or the reduction of stress, by staying in groups.

Q5

解析 原文提到长颈鹿妈妈会为了保护幼崽奋勇战斗，方式就是“向前和向后踢腿”（kicking），这就是在使用腿部防御。

干扰 “kicking”（踢）这个动作就等同于题目里的“use their legs”（用腿），别觉得题目换了个说法就找不到对应了。

句子 Giraffe calves are extremely vulnerable to predators, and though mothers will fight valiantly to keep their young alive — kicking forward and backward — half of all calves are killed in their first year of life.

Q6

解析 原文说年轻公鹿遇到更强大的老鹿时，会立刻试着让自己显得矮小无辜，而不是把脖子抬得更高。

干扰 你可能只看到了14句的“把头抬高”，但那是它们单独待着的时候，15句有个“But”转折，说明遇到强大的公鹿它们就认怂了。

句子 Recent observations show young bulls, when left on their own, mimicking their elders: head held high and neck puffed out. But should a dominant older bull come into view, the younger males instantly try to make themselves look small and innocent.

Q7

句子 Clashes have been witnessed between adults when each bull repeatedly ‘necks’ the other, using his massive neck to slam his head against his rival.

干扰 题目的“observed fighting”对应原文的“witnessed”（被目击）和“Clashes”（冲突/打斗），不要因为没看到长得一模一样的词就选错。

解析 原文提到人们曾目睹成年公鹿之间发生冲突，它们会用粗壮的脖子撞击对手，这说明它们打架的行为确实被观察到了。

Q8

解析 原文明确说长颈鹿皮毛上的斑块可以作为伪装（camouflage），让它们融入相思树的光影中。

干扰 题目要求填ONE WORD ONLY，定位到“serves as”后面，直接提取“camouflage”即可，不需要带上其他的多余词汇。

句子 The coat has dark patches separated by light hair, which serves as camouflage, allowing them to blend in with the light and shade patterns of the acacia trees from which they feed.

Q9

解析 原文提到长颈鹿的嘴唇和舌头能配合摘树叶，几乎就像人类用手（hands）抓取一样。

干扰 题目里有一个“like”（像），对应原文里的“as”，直接找作为比喻对象的名词填进去就可以了。

句子 In addition, a giraffe’s extraordinary mouth has lips and tongue that can together grasp a branch and then pluck away the leaves while avoiding thorns, almost as humans would grab with their hands.

Q10

句子 The growth of the neck largely takes place during early childhood, as giraffe mothers would have a difficult time giving birth to young with longer necks.

解析 原文说如果小鹿脖子太长，长颈鹿妈妈就很难分娩，所以脖子在出生后才长长，为的是让妈妈更容易生产（birth）。

干扰 题目里的“easier”对应原文的避免“difficult time giving birth”，所以提炼出分娩这个动作的名词“birth”即可。

Q11

解析 原文提到长颈鹿的静脉（veins）外部极厚，目的就是为了防止血液泄漏到周围组织中。

干扰 题目中的“extra-strong”对应原文的“extremely thick”，“keep...from spilling”对应“prevent...leaking”，找准对应的血管主语就可以了。

句子 The outside of a giraffe’s veins are extremely thick, to prevent blood leaking into surrounding tissue.

Q12

解析 原文指出研究人员惊讶地发现长颈鹿的心脏（heart）并没有大得异常，也就是对于这么大的动物来说，尺寸是正常的。

干扰 表格左侧要求填身体器官，原文“does not have an unusually large”（没有异常的大）就等于题目里的“normal size”，锁定心脏“heart”即可。

句子 Researchers were also surprised to find that a giraffe does not have an unusually large heart. It is half a percent of body mass, the same as in a mouse.

Q13

解析 原文解释说因为神经发出的信号（signals）在长颈鹿体内到达大脑的距离更远，所以它们反应比较慢。

干扰 第38句中的代词“they”指代的就是第37句里的主语“signals”，弄清楚代词指代什么就不会填错单词。

句子 This is because signals from the nerves travel at about the same speed in giraffes as in rats or other mammals. Given the greater distance they have to travel in the giraffe to reach the brain, it is possible the giraffe faces real challenges in reacting quickly to a rock beneath its hoof or a bite to its ankle.
